publication: local working tree; not released or deployed
scope: All and Disabled machine inventory filters
Policy-aware outbound source selection and cooldowns
Authenticated public/private control failover and relay source selection
Private relay status, actionable lease/clock errors and safe worker failure categories
Private dependency preparation during privileged Linux service setup
Automatic system hostname integration during privileged Linux enrollment/install and upgrades
Authselect/PAM preservation, NSS backups and rollback, and system getent readiness monitoring

cases: two default gateways with different metrics
interface down and recovery after host route restoration
isolated_namespace.isolation: Docker network=none, read-only filesystem, NET_ADMIN only, no writable host mount

additional_check_limitations: The existing inventory-pages.cjs browser suite was also attempted and failed at its unrelated proxy-binding editor assertion (0 list items versus 12 expected); the new standalone disabled-machines.cjs regression passed.
Cross-platform builds and live macOS/Windows source failover have not been validated here.
The pinned Rust toolchain encountered an incremental compiler failure; successful subsequent validation used CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0.
behavioral_boundaries: Automatic alternatives remain within the kernel-selected egress unless an explicit administrator preference or a validated PortHub-owned exit management bypass applies.
Gateway next-hop selection remains owned by the kernel; no automatic host route, address, DNS configuration or firewall repair.
macOS and Windows automatic mode conservatively retains the OS-selected source.
Public tunnels currently adopt the control source rather than selecting an independent source per tunnel origin.
Discovery is lazy with a 30-second cache and immediate failure invalidation.
Diagnosis distinguishes a live authenticated control check from saved public/private/relay observations.

Privileged enrollment now explicitly owns automatic DNS integration; the outbound selector and packet forwarding loops never modify DNS configuration. Check-only mode preserves administrator-managed settings.
